images.seen: Near East matches Cliopatria's Assyria (467k km2 empire), Babylonia, Elam and Hittite shapes; Hittite vassals tinted, Kaska contest stripes, Egypt direct to the Sudan and Canaan in vassal tint; no stray states

Elam wrongly kept eight Babylonian cells (seven round Babylon, one in the marshes) as a detached speck inside Iraq from 1158 on; Babylonia keeps a Zagros strip (Khuzestan 72, Ilam 64) that Elam's -1150 keyframe also claims, Susa stays Elam's

Before the patch Assyria was a 1,440-cell empire with stray Anatolian cells (2, 3 and 6 cells detached) while the Middle Assyrian page says it shrank to its heartland; Hittite land nobody's, Carchemish, Kammanu, Bit Bahiani and the Neo-Hittite states independent enclaves
Asia clean: Shang, Gandhara grave, Kuru with Painted Grey Ware, Kashi, Jorwe, Anau, Deng and Xi all compact and in the right regions; no speckle
Deng and Xi in the Henan-Hubei lowland south of Shang, each one compact blob in its own colour

Egypt now stops at 20 N, Canaan in vassal tint, Phoenicia and Philistia carved out; the Sudan blob and Dongola Reach cells are gone (before: 188 Sudanese cells held to -1151 and a detached 9-cell piece to the end)
Hole of 13 grey cells in the Argolid and 4 at Pylos inside Mycenaean Greece after the palace states ended; filled by events/2 and events/3
Assyria reduced to the heartland round Assur, Nineveh and Arbela; the northern enclaves stand on nobody's land; no stray Anatolian Assyrian cells

Tiglath-Pileser I's empire back in place (identical to the published draft at -1112 and at the end anchor), Phoenicia, Philistia, Edom and Moab as before, Egypt without Canaan, Elam and Babylonia whole

issues.what: Egypt kept the Dongola Reach (188 cells) and 48 Syrian cells (Damascus area) from -1200 to -1151, though the dossier loses the Dongola Reach at -1200: the 'wrong' keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1240 has the shape itself as its correction and was unioned into the keyframe of record at -1200..-1151, undoing the ledger's loss; the -1150 snap then removed 226 cells at once

A detached 9-cell piece of Egypt at 19.4 N 33.8 E (Nile bend by Abu Hamed) stayed Egyptian to the end of the window: the dossier's Nubia-intersect-box cut leaves out cells that the -1500 shape has but the gazetteer's Nubia lacks
Ten Egyptian cells in Lebanon (Beqaa 7, coast 3) stayed Egypt's direct land after Egyptian Canaan ended c. 1136

Elam held eight Babylonian cells (seven round Babylon, Babil 5 and Wasit 2, one marsh cell) from 1158 to the end: Elam's 1153 loss and Babylonia's 1153 gain use the gazetteer 'Babylonia' and the -1200 shape, both lacking cells that Babylonia held under the -1240 shape; a detached Elamite speck inside Iraq

Holes inside Mycenaean Greece: the carved-out palace states of Pylos (4 cells, ended -1180) and Mycenae (13 cells, ended -1150) left nobody's land in the Peloponnese until -1100, though Mycenaean Greece lasts to c. 1050 and Tiryns in the Argolid was the largest post-palatial centre

Assyria drawn as a 1,500-cell empire from -1200 to -1115 (Cliopatria shapes, dossier verdict ok because 'page silent on frontiers 1207-1115'); the Middle Assyrian Empire page gives 'First period of decline: c. 1206-1115 BC', says Assyria 'became restricted mostly to just the Assyrian heartland', Ninurta-apal-Ekur was 'unable to do much about the collapse of the empire', and puts the reconquest of northern Syria, the Mushki and the Euphrates in Tiglath-Pileser I's reign from 1114. Heartland now drawn -1200..-1115, empire shape from -1114 (same land as before at -1112 and at the end anchor); the dossier's -1150 gain (ledger 21) cancelled until 1114; also removes the stray Anatolian Assyrian cells and the Assyria/Isuwa, Assyria/Carchemish conflicts

Babylonia/Elam size-rule conflict at -1150 (Khuzestan 72, Ilam 64, Babylonia won): Babylonia's Kassite shape reaches into the Zagros foothills and Elam's corrected -1150 keyframe claims the same cells; Susa itself stays Elam's

Hittite collapse leaves most of Anatolia nobody's land from -1180 (Hittites, Tarhuntassa, Isuwa gone; Neo-Hittite states, Carchemish, Kammanu and Bit Bahiani as enclaves); Hayasa-Azzi ends -1200 with its land unowned

Size-rule conflicts where the smaller state rightly wins: carchemish, bit-bahiani, kammanu, kaska, moab, edom, phoenicia inside the larger shapes; kingdom-of-mycenae and kingdom-of-pylos carved out of Mycenaean Greece as the dossiers' notes intend
Kaska/Hittite contest (200 cells since -1430) closes in -1180 and Kaska ends -1112 with its land unowned; no contest or occupation left open
Asia in the window (Shang, Deng, Xi, Kuru, Painted Grey Ware, Gandhara grave, Jorwe, Kashi, Anau, Olmec, Americas and Japan cultures): compact and in the right regions, no holes or specks

problems: cross-window: keyframe_overrides/0 (new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1240, from -1240 to -1201, spec unchanged) reaches into m1300-m1201's years; it changes nothing there, but if the m1300-m1201 agent also overrides this shape_id their file wins (window order) and the Dongola and Syrian fix of -1200..-1151 is lost; m1300-m1201.json has no override of it when this report was written

cross-window: the Middle Assyrian page dates Assyria's decline from c. 1206, so the 1 January -1200 anchor still shows the empire and the loss is booked at -1200, six years late; the right place for the heartland is m1300-m1201's last years (-1206..-1201), which is not mine to write

the 1 January -1100 end anchor is unchanged for Assyria (empire shape from -1114, same cells as the published draft at -1112); the patch moves about 39 more cells at the end anchor, all Egypt (16), Mycenaean Greece (15) and Babylonia/Elam (8)

Assyria jumps from the heartland to the empire in -1114 (1,709 cells in one year), the accession year of Tiglath-Pileser I; the page calls his conquests 'ephemeral and shaky' and says western territories were 'likely lost again before his death', which the shapes of -1100..-1056 do not show
Second Dynasty of Isin page (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Dynasty_of_Isin) returned unrelated content and nothing usable; the Babylonia event rests on the Babylonia page instead
